rows.outcome: Positive effect in both matched pairs, rising with similarity
rows.evidence: K562 − Jurkat θ̂ ≈ 0; RPE1 − HepG2 θ̂ < 0; H4 slopes ≤ 0 where the own effect is nonzero.

rows.outcome: Effect in the mixed pairs only
rows.evidence: Mixed pooled θ̂ -0.0096 (CI [-0.0187, -0.00702]) is nonzero but negative, and a matched pair (RPE1 − HepG2) shows the same negative sign; gap mixed − matched -0.0042 (approx. CI [-0.00863, 0.000325], p 0.056).

rows.outcome: The generic response accounts for most of the raw difference
rows.evidence: Median generic share 2–13% per line in every pair.

rows.outcome: Naive tests find an effect; the main test does not
rows.evidence: Naive and main agree in sign and significance in 5 of 6 pairs; K562 − HepG2 (mixed): permutation-free naive tests p₂ 0.008–0.022 vs main 0.055. The naive step-7 estimate is not larger than the main one.

rows.outcome: No effect under any test, with adequate power
rows.evidence: θ̂ ≈ 0 under every test and sensitivity; planted detection limit 0.5% partial R²; pR²/rel upper bound 0.023%.

rows.outcome: Cross-line numbers sit near the same-line baseline
rows.evidence: K562 − Jurkat reproducible variance of M is 3.6× the same-line baseline (other pairs 43–154×); reliability 0.86.

K562 − Jurkat null; RPE1 − HepG2 significantly negative (opposite to H1). What differs: RPE1 − HepG2 still diverges at p53 targets (z 3.3) and every RPE1-containing pair shows the same promoter-driven negative association, while the three pairs without RPE1 do not.
Distal θ̂ weakly positive in the pairs without RPE1 (K562 − Jurkat one-sided p 0.021) but H2's non-overlap criterion fails in both matched pairs.

lead_with: pair-by-pair comparison of the two matched pairs (they disagree) with K562 − Jurkat's detection limit (null with adequate power) and RPE1 − HepG2's opposite-sign association traced to RPE1-containing pairs and residual p53 divergence
